title_card.title: Romans washed clothes in urine.
title_card.subtitle: Ammonia acted as a natural cleaning agent.

caption:
Ancient Romans used urine to wash their clothes.

Public collection vats were placed throughout ancient towns to gather urine for fullers who laundered wool fabrics. Historical records from 1912 documenting fulling workshops explain how ammonia broke down grease and dirt effectively.
